## ueh

`editor/ueh.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
ueh - Unreal Editor helpers for agent-driven editing. Runs inside UnrealEditor.

Pre-imported as `ueh` in every `ue.py py` call (the bridge reloads it when this file changes).
`ueh.help()` lists everything. Conventions:
  * "target" arguments accept an asset path (/Game/A/B or /Game/A/B.B), a loaded unreal.Object,
    or a level actor label. Blueprint asset paths resolve to the generated class's CDO for
    property access (props/get/set), and to the Blueprint itself everywhere else.
  * Rotations are (pitch, yaw, roll) tuples; locations are (x, y, z) tuples.
  * Nothing is saved unless a function says so (save=True or ueh.save()).
```

</details>

### `ueh.help(name=None)`

List helpers, or print the full doc of one helper: ueh.help('set').

### `ueh.project_modules()`

C++ module names declared in the .uproject.

### `ueh.cls(name)`

Resolve a class: unreal.Actor, 'RMRobot'/'ARMRobot', '/Script/Engine.Actor', or a Blueprint path.

### `ueh.find(path='/Game', cls=None, name=None, parent=None, recursive=True, limit=200)`

```text
Search the asset registry. cls: asset class name (e.g. 'Blueprint', 'StaticMesh');
name: substring of asset name; parent: substring of a Blueprint's parent class.
```

### `ueh.info(path)`

Asset summary: class, parent class, tags, dependency/referencer counts, dirty state.

### `ueh.deps(path, hard_only=False)`

Packages this asset depends on.

### `ueh.refs(path, hard_only=False)`

Packages that reference this asset.

### `ueh.asset(path)`

Load an asset (or return the object unchanged).

### `ueh.resolve(target, cdo=True)`

Object that property helpers operate on (BP asset -> its CDO when cdo=True; label -> actor).

### `ueh.prop_specs(target)`

{property_name: (type, access, doc)} for every editor-visible property of the object's native type.

### `ueh.props(target, filter=None, types=False)`

```text
Current values of editor properties (native ones; use get() for Blueprint-added variables).
filter: case-insensitive substring/regex on the name. types=True includes type and access.
```

### `ueh.get(target, prop_path)`

Read a property; dotted/indexed paths allowed: get('/Game/BP_X', 'mesh.static_mesh').

### `ueh.set(target, prop_path, value, save=False)`

```text
Set a property (on the CDO for Blueprint assets) with editor change notifications.
Nested paths set the final property on the owning sub-object; struct members are written back.
save=True saves the owning package.
```

### `ueh.export_text(target, cdo=True)`

T3D text of an object: every property incl. C++ UPROPERTYs and Blueprint variables (BP path -> CDO).

### `ueh.export_blueprints(out_dir, roots=('/Game',), skip=())`

```text
Export Blueprints, level Blueprints and data assets under `roots` to T3D/JSON in out_dir (for `ue.py bpdump`).
Per Blueprint: <name>.t3d, its CDO (<name>.cdo.t3d) and its parent class's CDO (<name>.parent.t3d).
Data assets, structs and enums -> <name>.t3d; data tables -> <name>.json. skip: package-path prefixes.
Loads (and so compiles) every Blueprint; saves nothing.
```

### `ueh.dirty()`

Package names with unsaved changes (maps + content).

### `ueh.save_object(obj)`

Save the package that owns an object.

### `ueh.save(*paths)`

Save the given assets (even if not dirty), or every dirty package when called with no args.

### `ueh.duplicate(src, dst)`

Duplicate an asset to a new path.

### `ueh.refresh_registry(root='/Game')`

```text
Bring the asset registry's dependencies up to date for packages saved this session. Right after a save the
registry still has a package's old dependencies (waiting for it doesn't help), so a rename or a validation run
would miss a referencer that was just saved. About 0.1 s per 1000 packages.
```

### `ueh.rename(src, dst)`

```text
Rename/move an asset. The engine loads, fixes and saves the referencers the asset registry knows about, and
leaves a redirector only when it can't. The registry is refreshed first: a referencer saved moments before
would otherwise be missed, and keep the old name on disk with no redirector behind it.
```

### `ueh.delete(path)`

Delete an asset. Refuses if something still references it unless forced via EAL directly.

### `ueh.fix_redirectors(path='/Game')`

```text
Fix up and remove redirectors under a folder (UETKEditor plugin; validate.fix_redirectors).
Returns {'fixed': [...], 'remaining': [...]}.
```

### `ueh.import_files(files, dest, replace=True, save=True)`

```text
Import source files (fbx/png/wav/...) into a content folder with the engine's defaults. Returns imported object
paths. importer.run adds kinds, presets, folders and reimport (`ue.py import`).
```

### `ueh.create_bp(parent, dest, save=True)`

Create a Blueprint (or Widget Blueprint for UserWidget parents) at dest from a parent class.

### `ueh.create_asset(dest, asset_class, factory, save=True)`

Generic asset creation, e.g. create_asset('/Game/Data/DA_X', unreal.DataAsset, unreal.DataAssetFactory()).

### `ueh.compile_bp(path)`

Compile one Blueprint. Compiler errors/warnings show up in the call's log output.

### `ueh.compile_bps(path='/Game', skip=())`

Load and compile every Blueprint under a folder (skip: path prefixes). Returns the count.

### `ueh.reparent_bp(path, new_parent, save=False)`

Change a Blueprint's parent class.

### `ueh.dt_json(path)`

Data table rows as parsed JSON.

### `ueh.dt_fill(path, rows, save=False)`

Replace a data table's rows from JSON text or a list of row dicts (each with a 'Name' key).

### `ueh.editor_world()`

The editor (non-PIE) world.

### `ueh.level()`

Path of the level open in the editor.

### `ueh.open_level(path)`

Open a level in the editor (fails if the current level has unsaved changes the editor wants to prompt about).

### `ueh.save_level()`

Save the current level.

### `ueh.actors(cls=None, name=None, limit=500, world=None)`

```text
Actors in the editor level, or with world='game' in the running game (PIE or a ue.py net process).
cls: substring of class name; name: substring of label/name.
```

### `ueh.actor(label, world=None)`

```text
Find an actor by exact label, then by object name, then by unique label substring: in the editor level, or
with world='game' in the running game.
```

### `ueh.spawn(class_or_path, location=(0, 0, 0), rotation=(0, 0, 0), label=None, world=None, props=None, owner=None, attach_to=None, socket=None, scale=None)`

```text
Spawn an actor from a class or Blueprint path: in the editor level, or with world='game' in the running game
(PIE, or a ue.py net process: spawn on the server and replicated actors reach the clients).
props {name: value} are set before the construction script and BeginPlay run in the game (expose-on-spawn
variables, any property); in the editor level they're set after. owner: an actor (or label) to own it;
attach_to: an actor (or label) to attach to, keeping the world transform, at socket.
```

### `ueh.move(label, location=None, rotation=None)`

Move/rotate a level actor.

### `ueh.destroy(*labels, world=None)`

Delete actors by label: from the editor level, or with world='game' from the running game.

### `ueh.select(*labels)`

Select level actors by label (no args clears the selection).

### `ueh.components(label)`

Components of a level actor: name, class, and attach parent.

### `ueh.camera()`

Editor viewport camera (location, rotation).

### `ueh.set_camera(location, rotation=(0, 0, 0))`

Move the editor viewport camera.

### `ueh.focus(label, distance=None)`

Point the editor viewport camera at an actor from a distance scaled to its bounds.

### `ueh.render_view(location=None, rotation=None, look_at=None, out=None, size=(1600, 900), fov=90.0, exposure=None, world=None, post=None)`

```text
Render a camera view of the editor level (or `world`) to PNG. Default camera: the level viewport's.
look_at=(x, y, z) aims the camera; exposure=None meters to mid-gray, a number fixes it (stops).
post: post-process material path(s) to apply (an outline, a colour grade).
```

### `ueh.render_pie(out=None, player_index=0, size=(1600, 900), exposure=None, post=None)`

```text
Render what a PIE player's camera sees (its location, rotation and FOV), offscreen. The game keeps running;
HUD/UMG is not included (render_widget(..., pie=True) draws those).
```

### `ueh.render_actor(label, out=None, yaws=None, pitch=-20.0, isolate=False, zoom=1.0, size=(800, 600), fov=50.0, exposure=None, columns=0, post=None)`

```text
Render a level actor from several angles (yaws relative to its facing; default four 3/4 views), framed to
its bounds. isolate=True draws only the actor. Works on PIE actors too (pass the object).
```

### `ueh.render_asset(path, out=None, yaws=None, pitch=-20.0, zoom=1.0, size=(800, 600), fov=50.0, exposure=None, floor=True, environment=True, columns=0, mesh=None, post=None)`

```text
Render an asset in a lit preview scene from several angles: static/skeletal mesh, material (a surface
material on `mesh`, a static mesh path, default a sphere; a post-process material over a sphere and a cube),
Blueprint actor, widget Blueprint (drawn at size), texture (its image). Niagara systems go to vfx.preview.
post: post-process material path(s) applied on top.
```

### `ueh.render_widget(target, out=None, size=(1920, 1080), background=(0.02, 0.02, 0.02), pie=False, world=None)`

```text
Render a UMG widget to PNG at a screen size (with the project's DPI scale): a Widget Blueprint path, a
widget class or instance. pie=True draws the live instance on screen in PIE (its real state); otherwise a
fresh one is created in the editor level, so anything it reads from the game is at its defaults.
```

### `ueh.is_pie()`

True while a Play-In-Editor session is running (always False in a game process).

### `ueh.pie_start(simulate=False)`

Request Play-In-Editor (or Simulate). Starts on a later frame; poll is_pie().

### `ueh.pie_stop()`

Request the end of the PIE session.

### `ueh.is_editor()`

True in the editor; False in a game process (`ue.py net` instances run UnrealEditor.exe -game/-server).

### `ueh.pie_world()`

The running PIE world (None when not playing). In a game process: the game world.

### `ueh.game_world()`

The world the game runs in: PIE's in the editor, the game's in a game process (None if there's none).

### `ueh.player(index=0)`

(player_controller, pawn) of a local player in the game world (PIE, or a game process).

### `ueh.console(command, pie=False)`

```text
Run a console command in the editor world, or in the game (PIE or a game process) via player 0 so cheat
Exec functions work. In a game process it always runs in the game.
```

### `ueh.key_down(key, value=None)`

```text
Start forcing a key: 'E', 'LeftMouseButton', 'SpaceBar', 'Gamepad_RightTrigger'. value: an axis value
(0.4, or 'X=5 Y=-3' for Mouse2D/2D axes). Stays down until key_up/release_all.
```

### `ueh.key_up(key)`

*(no docstring)*

### `ueh.release_all()`

Stop forcing every key these helpers pressed.

### `ueh.press(key, hold=0.08, value=None)`

```text
Scenario: `yield from ueh.press('R', 0.6)` holds a key for `hold` seconds of game time, then releases it
(also when the scenario is cancelled). The default 0.08 s is a tap.
```

### `ueh.mouse(dx, dy, seconds=0.25)`

```text
Scenario: `yield from ueh.mouse(5, -3, 0.5)` moves the mouse by (dx, dy) per frame for `seconds`, through the
mappings (Mouse XY 2D-Axis, e.g. IA_Look with its Negate and sensitivity modifiers).
```

### `ueh.action(name, value=True, seconds=None)`

```text
Force an input action's value each frame (skips the mappings' triggers/modifiers, unlike key_down). With
seconds, a scenario generator that releases it after that much game time; without, stays until -action.
```

### `ueh.net_info()`

```text
This process's network role and session: {role, map, players: [names], time}. Role is standalone,
listen_server, dedicated_server or client (a client that hasn't connected yet reports standalone).
```

### `ueh.game_time()`

Seconds of game time in the PIE world (None when not playing). Scenario waits count this.

### `ueh.wait(seconds)`

Scenario: `yield ueh.wait(5)` resumes after 5 s of PIE game time (wall clock outside PIE); `yield 5` is the same.

### `ueh.wait_real(seconds)`

Scenario: `yield ueh.wait_real(5)` resumes after 5 wall-clock seconds.

### `ueh.frames(count=1)`

Scenario: `yield ueh.frames(3)` resumes after 3 editor ticks (`yield` alone = 1).

### `ueh.until(predicate, timeout=60, message=None, interval=0)`

```text
Scenario: `value = yield ueh.until(lambda: ..., timeout=60)` resumes once predicate() is truthy and gets its value.

The predicate runs every tick (or every `interval` wall-clock seconds); after `timeout` wall-clock seconds a
TimeoutError is raised inside the scenario (catch it to carry on). `message` names the condition in that error.
```

## bpedit

`editor/bpedit.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
bpedit - edit Blueprint graphs from Python (UETKEditor plugin). Pre-imported as `bpedit` in `ue.py py`.

    g = bpedit.graph('/Game/BP_Door')                        # the event graph, or graph(path, 'MyFunction')
    begin = g.event('BeginPlay')                             # the existing override (enabled if it was a ghost) or new
    say = g.call('PrintString', InString='Door ready')       # pin literals as keywords
    g.chain(begin, say)                                      # exec wires: begin.then -> say.execute (and on)
    bpedit.add_variable('/Game/BP_Door', 'Health', 'float', 100, editable=True)
    hit = g.custom_event('TakeHit', Amount='float')
    hp, minus, set_hp = g.get('Health'), g.call('Subtract_DoubleDouble'), g.set_var('Health')
    g.link(hp, 'Health', minus, 'A'); g.link(hit, 'Amount', minus, 'B'); g.link(minus, 'ReturnValue', set_hp, 'Health')
    g.chain(hit, set_hp)
    print(g.text())                                          # nodes with ids, pins, literals and links
    bpedit.compile('/Game/BP_Door')                          # raises with the compiler's messages on errors

Nodes are addressed by id (g.text() / g.nodes() show them) or by a unique title; pins by name or display name,
ignoring case and spaces ('then', 'execute', 'True', 'ReturnValue', 'In String'). Types: bool, int, float, string,
name, text, vector, rotator, transform, a class (Actor, /Game/BP_X), object:X, class:X, struct:X, enum:X, array:T.
Nothing is saved: compile, then ueh.save(path) (ue.py save).
```

</details>

### `bpedit.blueprint(target)`

A Blueprint from a path or object.

### `bpedit.graph(bp, name='')`

A Graph to edit: the event graph by default, or a function/macro graph by name.

### `bpedit.graphs(bp)`

[{name, kind, nodes}] of a Blueprint, plus its parent class.

### `bpedit.add_variable(bp, name, type_, default=None, category='', editable=False, replicated=False, expose_on_spawn=False)`

Add a member variable (types as in the module docstring).

### `bpedit.add_function(bp, name, inputs=None, outputs=None, pure=False)`

Add a function graph with {name: type} inputs/outputs; returns its Graph (entry/result ids on .entry/.result).

### `bpedit.compile(bp, raise_on_error=True)`

Compile; returns {'status': ok|warnings|error, 'messages': [...]}, raising on errors by default.

### class `bpedit.BlueprintError` (RuntimeError)

*(no docstring)*

*(no docstring)*

#### `Node.title` (property)

*(no docstring)*

#### `Node.pins()`

*(no docstring)*

Set an unconnected input pin's literal.

### class `bpedit.Graph`

One graph of a Blueprint. Every method edits through the plugin and returns Node objects.

#### `Graph.nodes()`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.node(ident)`

A node by id or unique title (always freshly read, so positions and links are current).

#### `Graph.find(cls=None, title=None)`

Nodes whose class or title contains the given text.

#### `Graph.text()`

The graph as text: one block per node with its id, title, literals and links.

#### `Graph.call(function, cls=None, x=None, y=None, **literals)`

```text
A function call: PrintString, Delay, K2_DestroyActor/DestroyActor, Add_DoubleDouble... cls names the
owning class when it's not the Blueprint itself or a Kismet/GameplayStatics library.
```

#### `Graph.event(name, x=None, y=None)`

An overridable event (BeginPlay, Tick, ActorBeginOverlap, AnyDamage...): the existing one, or a new one.

#### `Graph.custom_event(name, x=None, y=None, **params)`

A custom event with parameters as keywords: custom_event('TakeHit', Amount='float').

#### `Graph.get(variable, cls=None, x=None, y=None)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.set_var(variable, cls=None, x=None, y=None, **literals)`

A variable Set node (named set_var so set() can stay the pin-literal setter).

#### `Graph.branch(x=None, y=None)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.sequence(x=None, y=None)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.self_ref(x=None, y=None)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.cast(cls, x=None, y=None)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.macro(name, x=None, y=None)`

A standard macro: ForEachLoop, ForLoop, WhileLoop, DoOnce, DoN, Gate, FlipFlop, IsValid...

#### `Graph.any_node(cls, x=None, y=None, **props)`

```text
Any graph node class, with properties (Unreal's text form, or asset paths) set before its pins are made:
any_node('K2Node_EnhancedInputAction', InputAction='/Game/Input/IA_Jump'). The class's module must be loaded.
```

#### `Graph.bound_event(component, event, x=None, y=None)`

```text
A widget's or component's event, as the editor's "+" buttons make it: bound_event('ResumeButton',
'OnClicked'), bound_event('TriggerBox', 'OnComponentBeginOverlap'). The existing one if there is one.
A widget added to a Widget Blueprint is a variable only after a compile.
```

#### `Graph.input_action(action, x=None, y=None)`

```text
An Enhanced Input action event, by path or asset name: exec outputs Triggered, Started, Ongoing,
Canceled and Completed, plus ActionValue (and its elapsed times).
```

#### `Graph.comment(text, x=0, y=0, width=400, height=200)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.link(a, a_pin, b, b_pin)`

```text
Wire a.a_pin to b.b_pin (a conversion node is added when the types need one). An automatically placed
exec node wired off an exec output moves to the right of it (lower for later outputs, e.g. a Branch's False).
```

#### `Graph.unlink(a, a_pin, b=None, b_pin='')`

Break one link, or every link of a.a_pin when b is None.

#### `Graph.chain(*nodes)`

```text
Wire the exec flow through the nodes in order (each one's first exec output to the next one's input),
and lay out the ones placed automatically to the right of their predecessor.
```

#### `Graph.tidy()`

```text
Move automatically placed data nodes (gets, math, conversions) to the left of the node that uses their
output, stacked by input order, so the graph reads left to right. chain() already lays out exec nodes.
```

#### `Graph.set(node, pin, value)`

Set an unconnected input pin's literal (numbers, bools, strings, 'x,y,z', enum names, asset paths).

#### `Graph.move(node, x, y)`

*(no docstring)*

#### `Graph.remove(node)`

*(no docstring)*

## mat

`editor/mat.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
mat - build and read materials from Python. Runs inside UnrealEditor; pre-imported as `mat` in `ue.py py`.

    mat.build(SPEC, '/Game/Materials/M_Rock')            # create, or rebuild in place; compile; save
    mat.describe('/Game/Materials/M_Rock')               # the graph as spec text (build() takes it back)
    mat.instance('/Game/Materials/MI_Rock_Red', '/Game/Materials/M_Rock', {'Tint': [1, .2, .2]})
    mat.function(SPEC, '/Game/Materials/MF_Tiling')      # a material function ('inputs' + 'out')
    mat.params('/Game/Materials/MI_Rock_Red')            # every parameter: type, value, overridden
    mat.preview('/Game/Materials/M_Rock', mesh='plane')  # PNG, offscreen (ueh.render_asset)
    mat.nodes('noise')                                   # material expression classes with their pins

Building uses the engine's MaterialEditingLibrary. Reading back (describe), compile errors, and the outputs Python
can't connect (pixel_depth_offset, shading_model, clear_coat...) need the UETKEditor plugin: `ue.py plugins install`.
Before UE 5.8 building needs it too (Python can't list a material's nodes or a node's outputs there). Compile errors
need a rendering editor: headless runs compile no shaders, and report errors=None.

SPEC (every key optional):
    {'domain': 'surface',          # surface | post_process | deferred_decal | light_function | volume | ui
     'blend': 'opaque',            # opaque | masked | translucent | additive | modulate | alpha_composite | alpha_holdout
     'shading': 'default_lit',     # default_lit | unlit | subsurface | clear_coat | two_sided_foliage | cloth | ...
     'two_sided': False,
     'usage': ['skeletal_mesh', 'niagara_sprites'],             # usage flags to switch on (MATUSAGE_*)
     'properties': {'opacity_mask_clip_value': 0.4,             # any Material property (snake_case or C++ name)
                    'blendable_location': 'after_tonemapping'},
     'params': {                   # parameters (instances override them), used by name in expressions
        'Tint': [1, 0.5, 0.2, 1],  #   vector
        'Roughness': 0.5,          #   scalar
        'Albedo': '/Game/T_Rock',  #   texture: sample(Albedo, uv)
        'Detail': True,            #   static switch: switch(Detail, a, b)
        'Speed': {'value': 1, 'group': 'Motion', 'min': 0, 'max': 5, 'desc': 'pan speed', 'priority': 1}},
     'let': {'uv': 'uv0 * Tiling'},                             # named steps, used by later lets and outs
     'out': {'base_color': 'sample(Albedo, uv).rgb * Tint', 'roughness': 'Roughness'}}
    Rebuilding replaces every node, and resets domain, blend, shading and two_sided to the spec's (or the defaults).

OUTPUTS: base_color metallic specular roughness anisotropy emissive opacity opacity_mask normal tangent
    world_position_offset subsurface_color ambient_occlusion refraction pixel_depth_offset shading_model clear_coat
    clear_coat_roughness displacement customized_uv0..7 material_attributes front_material

EXPRESSIONS (Python syntax):
    0.5, (1, 0, 0) constants; (uv.r, 0.5) appends; + - * / % ** ; 1 - x is a OneMinus node
    x.rgb, x.a, x.xy           swizzles (the node's own R/G/B/A/RGB/XY outputs when it has them, else a mask)
    x.Name                     one output pin by name: scene_texture(...).Size, fn(...).Result
    names                      params, lets, function inputs, and uv (uv0..uv7), time, world_pos, object_pos,
                               actor_pos, camera_pos, camera_dir, vertex_color, vertex_normal, pixel_normal,
                               screen_uv, pixel_pos, pixel_depth, scene_depth, object_radius, view_size,
                               particle_color, two_sided_sign, pi
    param('Base Color')        a parameter whose name isn't a Python name; input('UV Scale') likewise in functions
    sample(tex, uv)            tex: a texture param, an asset path '/Game/T_X', or a texture object. The sampler
                               type follows the texture (sRGB, normal map, masks); sampler='linear_color' overrides
    lerp(a, b, t) clamp(x, lo, hi) smoothstep(lo, hi, x) step(y, x) min max pow fmod atan2 dot cross distance
    saturate abs frac floor ceil round sign trunc sqrt exp log2 length normalize one_minus ddx ddy
    sin(x) cos(x)              radians (period 0); sin(x, period=1) is the editor's default Sine node
    fresnel(exponent, base, normal)  panner(uv, speed=(0.1, 0))  desaturate(color, fraction)  noise(pos, scale=0.1)
    transform(v, 'tangent', 'world')  transform_position(p, 'local', 'world')  compare(a, b, greater, equal, less)
    switch(Param, on, off)     a static switch parameter
    scene_texture('post_process_input0')            .Color (default), .Size, .InvSize
    custom('return A * B;', out='float3', A=x, B=y)  a Custom HLSL node (inputs in keyword order)
    fn('/Game/MF_X', x, Scale=2).Result              a material function call (inputs in order or by name)
    AnyNode(in1, in2, Prop=value)  any MaterialExpression class by name (SkyAtmosphereLightIlluminance,
                               RotateAboutAxis, ...): positional args feed its inputs in order (None skips one),
                               keywords feed an input with that name or set a property
    A number going into a node's input becomes that node's own constant (Add's ConstB, Lerp's ConstAlpha), not a
    Constant node. Repeated sub-expressions share one node.

FUNCTION SPEC (mat.function, or build() with 'function': True):
    {'inputs': {'UV': 'vector2', 'Scale': {'type': 'scalar', 'default': 1, 'desc': '...'}},   # in pin order
     'let': {...}, 'out': {'Result': 'input UV * Scale ...'},
     'description': '...', 'expose': True, 'categories': ['Custom']}
    Input types: scalar vector2 vector3 vector4 texture2d texture_cube texture2d_array volume_texture static_bool
    bool material_attributes.
```

</details>

### `mat.compile(target, wait=True)`

```text
Compile errors of a material or instance: {'errors': [...], 'error_nodes': [...], 'finished': bool}.
wait=True waits for the shaders (Custom HLSL errors only show up then). finished=False with no errors means it
wasn't compiled (headless runs compile no shaders). Needs the UETKEditor plugin.
```

### `mat.stats(target)`

Instruction and sampler counts of a material.

### `mat.build(spec, path, save_asset=True, check=True)`

```text
Create the material at `path` from a spec (dict or JSON text; see the module doc), or rebuild it in place
(every node replaced; references to it stay valid). Compiles, and saves unless save_asset=False.
Returns {path, nodes, params, errors (compile errors; [] = none), stats, saved}.
```

### `mat.function(spec, path, save_asset=True)`

```text
Create or rebuild a material function from a spec (module doc, FUNCTION SPEC). Saves unless save_asset=False.
Compile errors show in the materials that call it.
```

### `mat.params(target)`

Every parameter of a material or material instance: {name: {type, value, overridden (instances)}}.

### `mat.instance(path, parent=None, params=None, save_asset=True, reset=False, check=True)`

```text
Create or update a material instance: parent (a material or instance) is required when creating; params
{name: value} sets overrides (numbers, colour lists, texture paths, bools for static switches); reset=True
clears every override first. Saves unless save_asset=False.
```

### `mat.describe(target, text=True)`

```text
A material, material function or instance as its spec: build()/function()/instance() take it back.
text=True returns readable text, text=False the dict. Needs the UETKEditor plugin (except for instances).
```

### `mat.preview(target, mesh=None, out=None, **kwargs)`

```text
Render a material offscreen to PNG: surface materials on a mesh ('sphere' default, 'plane', 'cube',
'cylinder', 'cone' or a static mesh path), post-process materials over a sphere and a cube. Other options
go to ueh.render_asset (yaws, pitch, zoom, size, exposure, floor, environment).
```

### `mat.nodes(filter=None)`

```text
Material expression classes (for the AnyNode(...) syntax) with their input and output pins.
filter: case-insensitive substring of the class name.
```

### class `mat.MaterialError` (PropError)

*(no docstring)*

## inputs

`editor/inputs.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
inputs - Enhanced Input assets from Python: actions, mapping contexts, triggers and modifiers. Runs inside
UnrealEditor; pre-imported as `inputs` in `ue.py py`.

    inputs.build(SPEC)                                   # create or update actions and contexts, then save
    inputs.describe()                                    # every mapping context and action in /Game, as a SPEC
    inputs.describe('/Game/Input/IMC_Default')           # one context (or action)
    inputs.action('/Game/Input/IA_Sprint', 'bool')       # one action (type, triggers, modifiers, description)
    inputs.map_key('/Game/Input/IMC_Default', 'IA_Sprint', 'LeftShift', triggers=['hold'])
    inputs.unmap('/Game/Input/IMC_Default', action='IA_Sprint')       # or key='LeftShift', or both
    inputs.use_context('/Game/BP_PlayerController', '/Game/Input/IMC_Default')  # a Blueprint's default contexts
    inputs.add_context('/Game/Input/IMC_Vehicle', priority=1)          # in the running game (PIE / --instance)
    inputs.remove_context(...), inputs.active()          # which contexts the player has now
    inputs.keys('gamepad')                               # key names

SPEC (dict or JSON text):
    {'actions': {'/Game/Input/IA_Sprint': {'type': 'bool', 'triggers': ['down'], 'description': 'Run while held',
                                          'mappable': {'name': 'Sprint', 'display_name': 'Sprint',
                                                       'category': 'Movement'}},
                 '/Game/Input/IA_Move': 'axis2d'},
     'contexts': {'/Game/Input/IMC_Default': {
                     'mappings': {'IA_Sprint': ['LeftShift', 'Gamepad_LeftThumbstick'],
                                  'IA_Move': [{'key': 'W', 'modifiers': ['swizzle']},
                                              {'key': 'S', 'modifiers': ['swizzle', 'negate']}]},
                     'description': 'On foot', 'replace': False}}}
    An action listed under a context gets exactly those keys there; the context's other actions keep theirs unless
    'replace' is true. Actions are named by path, or by asset name when one InputAction (in the spec or the project)
    has it. Building an existing asset updates it in place, so references stay valid.
    Value types: bool, axis1d, axis2d, axis3d.
    Triggers: down pressed released hold hold_and_release tap pulse chord combo (or any InputTrigger class).
    Modifiers: negate swizzle dead_zone scalar response_curve smooth smooth_delta fov_scaling to_world_space
        scale_by_delta_time (or any InputModifier class).
    Each trigger or modifier is a name, or {name: {property: value}}: {'hold': {'hold_time_threshold': 0.5}},
        {'chord': {'chord_action': 'IA_Aim'}}, {'swizzle': {'order': 'zyx'}}, {'negate': {'x': False}},
        {'dead_zone': {'lower_threshold': 0.25}}.
    Keys are key names: W, SpaceBar, LeftShift, LeftMouseButton, Mouse2D, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom, Gamepad_Left2D,
        Gamepad_LeftThumbstick (the stick's button)... inputs.keys() lists them.
    Mappings in a context's per-profile overrides (5.7+) aren't read or written yet.
```

</details>

### `inputs.keys(filter=None)`

Key names (for mappings and ueh.press): filter is a case-insensitive substring ('gamepad', 'mouse').

### `inputs.map_key(context, action, key, triggers=None, modifiers=None, save_asset=True)`

Add one mapping to a context (keeps the others): map_key('/Game/Input/IMC_Default', 'IA_Sprint', 'LeftShift').

### `inputs.unmap(context, action=None, key=None, save_asset=True)`

Remove a context's mappings of an action, of a key, or of that action on that key. Returns how many went.

### `inputs.action(path, type=None, triggers=None, modifiers=None, description=None, mappable=None, save_asset=True, known=None, **props)`

```text
Create or update an InputAction. type: bool/axis1d/axis2d/axis3d; triggers/modifiers: spec items (module
doc); mappable: {'name', 'display_name', 'category'} makes it a player-mappable (rebindable) key setting;
other keywords set properties (consume_input, trigger_when_paused, accumulation_behavior...).
Triggers and modifiers given replace the action's own; None leaves them.
```

### `inputs.build(spec, save_asset=True)`

Create or update the actions and contexts of a spec (module doc). Returns what changed.

### `inputs.describe(target=None, text=True, root='/Game')`

```text
The project's input (every context and action under root), or one context or action, as a SPEC that build()
takes back. text=True returns readable text with where each context is used; False the dict.
```

### `inputs.use_context(blueprint, context, prop=None, save_asset=True, remove=False)`

```text
Put a mapping context in a Blueprint's input-context property (e.g. a player controller's
DefaultMappingContexts): appended to an array, or set. prop: the property name when there are several.
remove=True takes it out again.
```

### `inputs.add_context(context, priority=0, player=0)`

Add a mapping context to a local player in the running game (PIE or a ue.py net process).

### `inputs.remove_context(context, player=0)`

*(no docstring)*

### `inputs.active(player=0)`

The project's mapping contexts a local player has right now: {path: priority}.

### class `inputs.InputError` (PropError)

*(no docstring)*

## importer

`editor/importer.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
importer - bring source files into the project: static and skeletal meshes, animations, textures and sounds, with
presets. Runs inside UnrealEditor (or headless); pre-imported as `importer` in `ue.py py`.

    importer.run(['D:/Art/Props', 'D:/Art/SM_Rock.fbx'], '/Game/Props')   # files and folders (folders recursively)
    importer.run('D:/Art/A_Run.fbx', '/Game/Anims', skeleton='/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton')
    importer.run('D:/Art/T_Rock_ORM.png', '/Game/Props', texture='masks')  # presets come from the name; this overrides
    importer.reimport('/Game/Props')            # every asset there whose source file changed since its import
    importer.sources('/Game/Props')             # each imported asset's source file, and whether it changed

What each file becomes:
    .fbx            static mesh, skeletal mesh or animation, from its content (polygons, skin clusters, bones, curves)
                    unless the name says (SM_, SK_/SKM_, A_/AS_/Anim_) or kind= does
    .obj            static mesh            .gltf .glb   whatever the file holds (the engine's glTF importer)
    .png .jpg .jpeg .tga .bmp .tif .tiff .psd .exr .hdr .dds   texture
    .wav .ogg .flac .aif .aiff                                 sound
Texture presets (texture=, or from the name's last _suffix): color (default: _D _BaseColor _Albedo...), normal (_N
    _Normal _Nrm), masks (_ORM _ARM _RMA _M _R _AO _Rough _Metal _Mask...), grayscale (_H _Height _Disp _Opacity),
    linear, hdr (.exr .hdr), ui. A dict sets texture properties directly: {'srgb': False, 'lod_group': 'ui'}.
Options (keywords, or rules=[{'match': '*_UI_*.png', 'texture': 'ui'}] per file name):
    kind='static'|'skeletal'|'animation'   materials=True  textures=True (from the mesh file)
    skeleton=PATH (skeletal: share one; animation: required)   physics_asset=True   animations=False (in a mesh file)
    collision=True|False|'box'|'sphere'|'capsule'|'convex'|'complex'|'none'   combine=True   normals='import'|'compute'|
    'import_tangents'   scale=1.0   nanite=None   lightmap_uvs=None   lod_group=None (static mesh LOD group)
    looping=None  sound_class=PATH  attenuation=PATH  volume=None (sounds)
    name=  (one file: the asset name; default the file name)   flat=False (folders: don't mirror subfolders)
Every imported asset records its source file and the options in its package metadata (tag UETK.Import), so
reimport() repeats the same import, and sources() tells which source files changed (by content hash).
```

</details>

### `importer.classify(path, options=None)`

What a source file will become: {'type': mesh|texture|sound, 'kind', 'why'} (raises for unknown types).

### `importer.run(paths, dest, rules=None, save=True, flat=False, **options)`

```text
Import files and folders (recursively) into dest; subfolders are mirrored unless flat=True. Options and
presets are in the module doc; rules=[{'match': glob on the file name, ...options}] override them per file.
Returns one record per file: source, kind and why, the assets made ('new' or 'replaced'), presets applied,
or 'error'. A file that fails doesn't stop the others.
```

### `importer.sources(target='/Game')`

```text
Each toolkit-imported asset under target (or one asset): its source file, and whether that file is missing,
changed (different content) or unchanged since the import.
```

### `importer.reimport(target='/Game', all=False, save=True)`

```text
Import again, with the options recorded at import, every toolkit-imported asset under target (or one asset)
whose source file changed; all=True reimports unchanged ones too. Returns the import records.
```

### `importer.report(result)`

run()/reimport() records or sources() as readable lines.

### class `importer.ImportFailed` (PropError)

*(no docstring)*

## ui

`editor/ui.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
ui - UMG menus and HUDs: read and drive the widgets on screen in a running game, and build Widget Blueprints from a
spec. Runs inside UnrealEditor or a ue.py net game process; pre-imported as `ui` in `ue.py py`. Needs the UETKEditor
plugin (Python can't reach a widget tree's root).

In the running game (PIE, or `ue.py --instance client1 ...`):
    print(ui.tree())                    # every widget on screen: class, name, text, enabled, rectangle in pixels
    ui.click('Resume')                  # a button (or checkbox) by its label or name, as a real click fires it
    ui.type('PlayerName', 'Ada')        # an editable text: set, changed, committed (Enter)
    ui.set('Volume', 0.3)               # slider, spin box, checkbox, combo box
    ui.text('Status'), ui.text()        # one widget's text, or all text on screen
    ui.find('Resume')                   # the widget object
    ui.open('/Game/UI/WBP_Inventory')   # put a widget on screen (Create Widget + Add to Viewport)
    yield ui.wait('Paused')             # in a scenario: until it's on screen (gone=True: until it isn't)
Targets match a widget's name, or its label (its text, or the text inside it, ignoring case): exactly first, then
the start of the label, then anywhere in it. A button and the text inside it share a label; the button wins. Only
widgets on screen count unless hidden=True. player=N picks a local player's widgets.
Rectangles (tree()) need the game view to have been painted: an editor in the background doesn't paint its PIE
viewport, so they're left out there.
Clicks, typing and values go through the widgets' own events (OnPressed, OnReleased, OnClicked; OnTextChanged,
OnTextCommitted; OnValueChanged...), so Blueprint and C++ handlers run as for a real click. They don't go through
Slate's hit testing: a button covered by another widget still gets clicked.

Building Widget Blueprints (the designer tree):
    ui.build(SPEC, '/Game/UI/WBP_PauseMenu')   # create, or rebuild the tree in place; compiles and saves
    print(ui.describe('/Game/UI/WBP_PauseMenu'))
    g = bpedit.graph('/Game/UI/WBP_PauseMenu'); g.bound_event('ResumeButton', 'OnClicked')   # its event graph
SPEC: {'parent': 'UserWidget',            # the parent class (only used when creating)
       'root': {'type': 'CanvasPanel', 'name': 'Root', 'children': [
           {'type': 'VerticalBox', 'name': 'Menu',
            'slot': {'anchors': [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5], 'alignment': [0.5, 0.5], 'auto_size': True},
            'children': [
                {'type': 'TextBlock', 'name': 'Title', 'text': 'Paused', 'font_size': 36},
                {'type': 'Button', 'name': 'ResumeButton', 'text': 'Resume', 'slot': {'padding': 8}},
                {'type': 'CheckBox', 'name': 'InvertY', 'props': {'checked_state': 'checked'}}]}]}}
    type: any widget class (TextBlock, Button, Image, Border, SizeBox, CanvasPanel, VerticalBox, HorizontalBox,
          Overlay, ScrollBox, CheckBox, Slider, ProgressBar, EditableTextBox, ComboBoxString, SpinBox, Spacer...)
          or a Widget Blueprint path. Every widget is a variable, so the graph can use it.
    text: a TextBlock's text; on a Button, a TextBlock inside it. font_size, color ([r, g, b, a] linear) for text.
    props: any property (snake_case or C++ name). slot: canvas slots take position, size, anchors ([min x, min y,
          max x, max y]), alignment, auto_size, z_order; box and overlay slots take padding (a number or [l, t, r, b]),
          h_align / v_align (left|center|right|fill, top|center|bottom|fill), fill (a weight; omit for auto size).
```

</details>

### `ui.tree(player=None, hidden=False, text=True)`

```text
The widgets on screen as an indented outline (text=False: a list of dicts): class, name, text or value,
disabled, and the rectangle in viewport pixels [x, y, width, height].
```

### `ui.find(target, player=None, hidden=False)`

The widget object a target names (module doc: by name or label).

### `ui.click(target, player=None)`

```text
Click a button or checkbox by label or name: OnPressed, OnReleased and OnClicked fire, as for a real click (a
checkbox toggles and fires OnCheckStateChanged). Returns what was clicked.
```

### `ui.type(target, text, commit=True, player=None)`

Type into an editable text: its text is set, OnTextChanged fires, and (commit=True) OnTextCommitted with Enter.

### `ui.set(target, value, player=None)`

Set a slider, spin box (a number), checkbox (a bool) or combo box (an option), firing its change event.

### `ui.text(target=None, player=None)`

One widget's label (its text, or the text inside it), or every text on screen, top to bottom.

### `ui.open(widget, player=0, z_order=0)`

```text
Put a user widget on screen in the running game, as Create Widget + Add to Viewport do: a Widget Blueprint
path or a widget class, owned by local player `player`. Returns the widget.
```

### `ui.wait(target, timeout=10.0, gone=False, player=None)`

```text
Scenario: `yield ui.wait('Paused')` resumes when a widget matching target is on screen (gone=True: when none
is) and returns it. Timed in wall-clock seconds, so a paused game doesn't stall it.
```

### `ui.build(spec, path, save=True)`

```text
Create a Widget Blueprint from a spec (module doc), or rebuild an existing one's designer tree in place (its
graph stays; references to it stay valid). Compiles and saves. Returns {path, widgets, compile}.
```

### `ui.describe(path, text=True)`

```text
A Widget Blueprint's designer tree: each widget's type, name, text, non-default properties and slot settings.
text=False returns the dict (a SPEC whose props and slots are in Unreal's own property names).
```

### class `ui.UIError` (PropError)

*(no docstring)*

## validate

`editor/validate.py`

<details><summary>Module notes</summary>

```text
validate - project checks for scripts, commit hooks and CI (`ue.py validate`). Pre-imported as `validate`.

    validate.run()                                         # the default checks on /Game
    validate.run(['/Game/UI'], checks=['data', 'blueprints'])
    print(validate.report(validate.run()))                 # the text `ue.py validate` prints
    validate.fix_redirectors('/Game')                      # resave referencers, delete the redirectors

run() returns {'findings': [...], 'counts': {'error': n, 'warning': n, 'info': n}, 'failed': bool,
'checked': {check: how many}, 'skipped': {check: why}, 'seconds': {check: s}}. A finding is
{'severity': 'error'|'warning'|'info', 'check', 'asset', 'message'}.

Checks (* = on by default):
  references*  references to packages that don't exist. Hard references are errors (the asset loads with the
               reference cleared), soft ones warnings.
  redirectors* leftover redirectors (warnings). fix_redirectors() fixes them (UETKEditor plugin).
  textures*    textures over max_texture_size on a side (default 4096; virtual textures exempt), and textures whose
               sides aren't powers of two outside the UI group (they get no mips and don't stream; importing
               sets such a texture to "no mipmaps" itself).
  blueprints*  compiles every Blueprint (Widget, Anim, Editor Utility...): the compiler's errors and warnings
               (UETKEditor plugin).
  data*        Data Validation, as the Content Browser's Validate Assets runs it: the engine's and the project's
               validators and each asset's IsDataValid (UETKEditor plugin). Loads every asset it checks.
  maps*        map check on `maps` (paths, or 'all' for every map under the roots), else the level open in the
               editor (UETKEditor plugin). In an editor window the open level comes back afterwards.
  unused       assets nothing references: info, a lead to follow. Maps, Editor Utilities and assets whose path
               appears under Config/ or Source/ aren't reported; code that builds paths at runtime isn't seen.
  naming       name prefixes by asset class (warnings): `naming: true` (or asking for the check by name) for
               NAMING below, or {class: prefix(es)}.

Settings come from <Project>/.uetk/validate.json, and keyword arguments to run() override them:
  {"roots": ["/Game"], "exclude": ["/Game/Developers"], "checks": {"unused": true, "data": false},
   "max_texture_size": 4096, "maps": ["/Game/Maps/Main"], "naming": true,
   "ignore": [{"check": "textures", "asset": "/Game/Sky/*"}, {"message": "*deprecated*"}],
   "fail_on": "error"}
`checks` may also be a list (exactly those). `ignore` entries match findings by fnmatch patterns on any of check,
asset, message and severity. fail_on: "error" (default) or "warning".
```

</details>

### `validate.settings(**overrides)`

The project's .uetk/validate.json merged with keyword overrides (None values ignored).

*(no docstring)*

*(no docstring)*

*(no docstring)*

*(no docstring)*

```text
Run the checks (see the module docstring) and return the findings. Settings: .uetk/validate.json, then
```

### `validate.report(result, limit=None)`
